meta.note: Illustrative game content, not immigration advice. Lagos Life from the Cursor build; pitch, tourist and LMIA routes from the Japa engine.

items.title: IELTS speaking: Band 5.5
items.body: The examiner asked about your hometown. Village People Interference scrambled the answer. The recording is already on a server in Cambridge.

items.title: Landlord ghosted you
items.body: The viewing was at 4. The gate man has not seen anyone. Your deposit is a voice note that will never be opened.

items.title: '100% guaranteed visa, ₦8.5m'
items.body: A smooth agent in a nice office promises a Canada work visa, half upfront. Your cousin paid him last year. Your cousin is still here.

items.title: Passport appointment moved again
items.body: The passport office reschedules for the third time. Your police certificate will expire before the booklet is ready.

items.title: 'Canada needs 650,000 workers, share to 10 groups'
items.body: Your aunty forwarded it with three prayer emojis. Fact-checkers debunked it years ago. Seasonal farm programs don't even take Nigerians.

items.title: Papa wants to sell the village land
items.body: The family meeting agrees to sell the plot for your japa. Everyone is proud. Everyone will remember.

marketShock.title: The rate just moved.
marketShock.body: The parallel market rate jumped to naira 1,800/$! Your proof of funds has lost 25% of its purchasing power overnight.

ranks.title: Flagged at the VAC
ranks.blurb: The account name was your friend's. The five-year bar is real, and no danfo goes around it.

ranks.title: Vanier Scholar
ranks.blurb: The committee saw the file. The fire stayed lit. {RelName} in {relCity} is already buying you a winter coat that is too optimistic.

ranks.title: Deported at Pearson Airport
ranks.blurb: You cleared {airportCode}. Canada did not clear you. The officer stamped the dream on the way back to the gate.

ranks.title: Village People Took the Call
ranks.blurb: Interference hit critical. IELTS, landlords, and a cousin in the group chat finished the route for you.

ranks.title: Still on the Corridor
ranks.blurb: Not Pearson. Not Vanier. {area} still knows your name. The next danfo is boarding.

ranks.title: Graduate with a PGWP
ranks.blurb: Degree done, work permit approved. Canadian experience starts Monday.

ranks.title: Flagged for misrepresentation
ranks.blurb: Fake letters and parked money get checked. The five-year bar is real.

ranks.title: Refused, for now
ranks.blurb: A stronger study plan is the usual fix. Rewrite it and apply again.

ranks.title: Out of status
ranks.blurb: Cash shifts felt like a shortcut. The study permit had conditions.

ranks.title: Back to the plan
ranks.blurb: Not this term. The library still knows your name.

items.title: The basement room was never real
items.body: CAD 1,200 deposit to a 'landlord' on Kijiji who was 'out of the country, will mail the keys'. The keys are still in the mail.

items.title: Daddy's transfer arrived smaller
items.body: Same naira, fewer dollars. Rent did not get the memo.

items.title: Shifts cut
items.body: The warehouse cut part-timers to 10 hours. Students are allowed 24 a week; nobody is guaranteed any.

items.title: Group project ghost
items.body: Your group of four is a group of one. The deadline is Friday.

items.title: Your program was suspended
items.body: The college cut 40 programs after international enrolment fell. Yours is one of them. You transfer and update your permit; the paperwork costs a month.

items.title: Mummy needs money
items.body: CAD 300 for a relative's hospital bill, between pay cheques. You send it. You eat noodles until Friday.

items.title: Japa to sapa
items.body: The campus food bank has no sign on the door and no questions. You go. You don't post it.

ranks.title: Permanent Resident
ranks.blurb: ITA, eAPR, COPR. Welcome to Canada. The winter coat is not optional.

ranks.title: Ghosted IRCC
ranks.blurb: They wrote first. You didn't answer. Refused.

ranks.title: Flagged for misrepresentation
ranks.blurb: Shortcuts end in five-year bans. Every point has to be real.

ranks.title: Plan B: the classroom
ranks.blurb: Canadian education plus Canadian work is the strongest Express Entry profile there is.

ranks.title: The pool can wait
ranks.blurb: Rest first. Profiles last a year.

ranks.title: Still in the pool
ranks.blurb: Not this round. The next draw is in two weeks.

items.title: The naira slipped again
items.body: Your savings are the same number of naira and fewer dollars. Proof of funds is counted in Canadian dollars.

items.title: Courier lost your transcript
items.body: Tracking says 'delivered' to an address in Mississauga that is a car wash. The registry wants another fee and another month.

items.title: No draw for six weeks
items.body: The rounds page has not moved since the 3rd. Telegram groups say the system is 'under review'. Telegram groups say a lot of things.

items.title: Happy birthday
items.body: Cake, candles, and a quiet drop in your age points. Every year past 29 costs you on the calculator.

items.title: One band short
items.body: L8 R7 W6.5 S7. Writing missed CLB 9 by half a band, about 20 points. The retake costs ₦279,500.

items.title: ASUU strike, registry closed
items.body: Your transcript can't leave the university until the strike ends and an old bursary hold is cleared. WES won't accept copies you carry yourself.

items.title: Telegram says a draw is coming
items.body: Three hundred people refresh the rounds page at 2 p.m. Ottawa time. It is a French draw. You do not speak French.

TOURIST_GAMBLE.title: The 180-Day Tourist Gamble
TOURIST_GAMBLE.tagline: 180 days. No work. Wey Sabi says Kawosoke.

ranks.title: Protected person
ranks.blurb: Your real story, told straight, with evidence. Next stop: permanent residence. Don't renew that green passport.

ranks.title: Boardroom bound
ranks.blurb: Three leads in 180 days without working a single illegal shift. Mr. Kovacs is waiting.

ranks.title: Bought story, sold dream
ranks.blurb: The paralegal sold the same page forty times. The board noticed. Five-year bar, removal, and the real ones get believed less.

ranks.title: CAD 25k for a PDF
ranks.blurb: Positive LMIA, negative bank balance.

ranks.title: Cash job, CBSA tip
ranks.blurb: Eight shifts, one angry co-worker, one removal order.

ranks.title: Village People: not a Convention ground
ranks.blurb: The board was very polite about the juju. Refused.

ranks.title: Believed, but 'try Port Harcourt'
ranks.blurb: Internal flight alternative: the most Nigerian refusal there is.

ranks.title: Refused on credibility
ranks.blurb: Three versions of one night. Appeal, Federal Court, PRRA, then a removal date.

ranks.title: Went home for the party
ranks.blurb: Flew back to the country you said you feared. The claim did not survive the owambe.

ranks.title: Time's up
ranks.blurb: 180 days of LinkedIn. The return ticket wins.

ranks.title: Uncle Couch
ranks.blurb: The kids still ask when you are coming back.

items.title: Moved to a hotel in Niagara Falls
items.body: The shelter is full. A bus takes you two hours from the clinic that has your file. Tourists are taking selfies by the falls; you are taking the 6 a.m. GO bus.

items.title: Wey Sabi wants a 'consultation fee'
items.body: Three coffee chats, apparently, were billable. CAD 300 by Friday or Wey Sabi tells the whole church you are 'ungrateful'.

items.title: Your story, as remembered by your cousin
items.body: Your cousin told the family group your claim details 'for prayer'. Now four aunties have four versions, and one of them is on Facebook.

items.title: First real snowstorm
items.body: You missed the clinic appointment because the bus did not come and your shoes are canvas. You rebook for three weeks later.

lessons.OUT_OF_MONEY: Visitors must show they can support themselves for the whole stay. Most people underestimate rent, transit and winter clothes in their first months.
lessons.STAY_EXPIRED: Visitors are usually allowed up to six months. You can apply to extend before your status expires; staying past it without applying makes you out of status.
lessons.BURNOUT: Job hunting without the right to work is exhausting. Settlement agencies, libraries and newcomer job programs are free, and most are open to visitors.
lessons.UNAUTHORIZED_WORK: Working as a visitor, even cash shifts or an 'unpaid trial', is unauthorized work. It can lead to removal and make future applications fail.

FIRST_YEAR.title: Year One in Canada
FIRST_YEAR.tagline: You landed. Now the real japa starts.

items.title: The basement flooded
items.body: Spring thaw, a sump pump older than you, and your Ankara now smells like a swimming pool. The landlord says it is 'an act of God'.

items.title: The landlord's nephew needs the unit
items.body: Suddenly there is a nephew. Moving again costs a weekend, a truck and another first-and-last.

items.title: The newcomer phone promo ended
items.body: Your CAD 35 plan is now CAD 75. Nobody read the fine print, least of all you.

items.title: Church potluck jollof, and a lead
items.body: Someone's aunty tastes your jollof, approves, and mentions her company is hiring. Referrals: the hidden job market.

items.title: Your first credit card: limit CAD 500
items.body: No credit history, so the bank starts you small. Paying it in full every month is how the score grows.

ranks.title: Back in your field
ranks.blurb: Bridging, networking and a referral from a potluck. The LinkedIn post writes itself.

ranks.title: Surviving, not thriving
ranks.blurb: Bills paid, family helped, career on pause. Year two is when it turns, if you plan it.

ranks.title: Japada: reverse japa
ranks.blurb: You went home. The group chat will talk. You will sleep.

ranks.title: Year One won
ranks.blurb: Out of money, out of energy, out of you. Settlement agencies are free; ask earlier next time.

lessons.BURNOUT: Newcomers in their first five years have had far higher unemployment than people born in Canada. Settlement agencies, food banks, EI and free counselling exist for the hard months; using them is not failure.

LAGOS_YABA_DAWN.title: Generator coughs. Light dies.
LAGOS_YABA_DAWN.speaker: {area}, {city}
LAGOS_YABA_DAWN.dialogue: NEPA has packed up. Your roommate is already in a Europe group chat. Downstairs, {area} is waking. {RelWho} in {relCity} sent three missed calls. Japa this year, or watch another circle leave.

choices.text: {Bus} to {techHub} and hunt remote jobs
Call {relTitle} in {relCity} about the visa story
Sleep. Trek the street when dusk is cheaper.

LAGOS_JOB_BOARD.title: Four hundred applicants. One reply.
LAGOS_JOB_BOARD.speaker: {techHub}
LAGOS_JOB_BOARD.dialogue: The cyber cafe hums like a generator. A Toronto listing wants three years of React and right to work in Canada. You have a bootcamp PDF, stubborn data, and {relName} typing 'have you left the house??' from {relCity}.

choices.text: Rewrite the CV like you already live in Zone 2
{Bus} to the visa consultant blasting your status
Trek back to {area} and rethink the whole plan

LAGOS_AUNTY_CALL.title: {RelName} does not sugarcoat.
LAGOS_AUNTY_CALL.speaker: {relCity} × {area} FaceTime
LAGOS_AUNTY_CALL.dialogue: {RelPoss} window in {relCity} shows {relWeather}; {relSubj} is {relGap}. Yours is generator light. {RelSubj} will write an invitation letter. {RelSubj} will not lie on a bank statement. 'Bring your own proof, {name}, or don't come and disgrace me at Pearson.'

choices.text: Leave the call. Trek the annex and start a real paper trail
Ask her to lend you the showing-money

LAGOS_YABA_DUSK.title: The street is louder than your plan.
LAGOS_YABA_DUSK.speaker: {market}, at the edge
LAGOS_YABA_DUSK.dialogue: Pepper soup steam, {bus} horns, a preacher on a megaphone. People are going somewhere: work, church, the park, abroad in their heads. {RelName}'s last voice note is still unplayed.

choices.text: Catch another {bus} to the job hunt
Step aside and call {relName} properly
Okada to a weekend gig in {gigArea}

LAGOS_CV_NIGHT.title: The document starts to look like a person.
LAGOS_CV_NIGHT.speaker: {area} room, 3 a.m.
LAGOS_CV_NIGHT.dialogue: You quantify the internships. You hide the generator. A recruiter in Toronto replies. {RelName} is on a night shift in {relCity}; {relPoss} status still says 'call me when light comes.'

choices.text: Take the interview. Buy data. Set two alarms.
Ghost it and go back to the street

LAGOS_AGENT_OFFICE.title: The office smells like toner and panic.
LAGOS_AGENT_OFFICE.speaker: Agent's office, {city}
LAGOS_AGENT_OFFICE.dialogue: He talks fast: Schengen, Canada express, 'we know people'. {RelName} would shout if {relSubj} saw this receipt. Your folder is heavier. Your stomach is not.

choices.text: Pay 'facilitation' then {bus} to the visa centre
Walk out. Trek the annex with a clean file

LAGOS_DOCUMENT_GRIND.title: Photocopies, stamps, another queue.
LAGOS_DOCUMENT_GRIND.speaker: Immigration annex, Alausa
LAGOS_DOCUMENT_GRIND.dialogue: Bodies in a line that does not move and also never ends. A clerk calls names like a {bus} conductor. {RelName} texts a photo of the invitation letter, snow on the window behind {relObj}.

choices.text: Book the appointment. {Bus} to the visa centre
Envelope too thin. Okada to the weekend hustle

LAGOS_SHOWING_MONEY.title: Love, with conditions.
LAGOS_SHOWING_MONEY.speaker: WhatsApp: {relName} & the family group
LAGOS_SHOWING_MONEY.dialogue: {RelName} will send a statement snapshot, not a transfer. 'If they ask whose money, tell the truth.' Uncle in Abuja laughs from the group chat: Canada is for people with uncles in Canada.

choices.text: Hang up. Build an honest file at the annex
Borrow a friend's statement and go anyway
choices.label: MISREPRESENTATION
choices.feedback: Submitting someone else's bank statement as your own is misrepresentation.

LAGOS_WEEKEND_GIG.title: Cash in the pocket. Dust in the lungs.
LAGOS_WEEKEND_GIG.location: Rain in {gigArea}, then the okada home
LAGOS_WEEKEND_GIG.speaker: Rain in {gigArea}, then the okada home
LAGOS_WEEKEND_GIG.dialogue: You fix a POS network, then two Bolt trips in the rain. The envelope thickens. A woman under a shop awning is shouting into her phone the same way you shout to {relName}: 'I am coming. Traffic.'

choices.text: Bank it. {Bus} to the paperwork
Trek home and spend some on a better portfolio
One more weekend. Trek back to {area}.

LAGOS_BERLIN_CALL.title: 7:03 a.m. The call connects.
LAGOS_BERLIN_CALL.speaker: {area}, on borrowed light
LAGOS_BERLIN_CALL.dialogue: Toronto asks about a race condition you actually fixed. Then they ask if you can fly. {RelName} is on speaker from a {relCity} bus: 'Say yes. I will be waiting at Pearson.'

choices.text: Use the offer as the spine. {Bus} to the visa centre
Panic. Go back to the street and call {relName} later

LAGOS_EMBASSY_QUEUE.title: The queue is a weather system.
LAGOS_EMBASSY_QUEUE.speaker: Visa Application Centre, {vacCity}
LAGOS_EMBASSY_QUEUE.dialogue: Plastic chairs. Names like a lottery. A man in front is whispering to his brother in Houston. You hold {relName}'s letter like it can stand in the line for you.

choices.text: Answer every question like the form already knows you
Over-explain. Fill silences. Offer extra papers.

LAGOS_DECISION_GATE.title: They take the passport. You take the wait.
LAGOS_DECISION_GATE.speaker: Outside the centre, VI sun
LAGOS_DECISION_GATE.dialogue: You step into the heat. {RelName} is already ringing. Tracking sites lie. WhatsApp groups lie louder. You go home and live inside a status page.

choices.text: Pick {relName}'s call, then wait with the phone on loud

LAGOS_OUTCOME.title: A text at 11:41 p.m.
LAGOS_OUTCOME.speaker: {area} mattress, phone glowing
LAGOS_OUTCOME.dialogue: {RelName} is typing. The embassy mail is sitting unopened. If the file and the spirit held, the country lets you leave. If not, you are still here — which is not the same as finished.

choices.text: Open the email. Call {relName} either way.

LAGOS_ENDING_WIN.title: You japa.
LAGOS_ENDING_WIN.speaker: Airside, {airportCode} → the glass
LAGOS_ENDING_WIN.dialogue: Plastic tray. Stamped page. {RelName} is on FaceTime from Pearson arrivals in a future you have not reached yet, and also from {relCity} right now, crying and laughing. You go. That is the deal.

outcome.title: You japa
outcome.lesson: A visa in the passport is permission to travel, not to stay. The officer at the Canadian port of entry still decides, and your status is only as good as the reason you gave.

LAGOS_ENDING_STAY.title: The country keeps you.
LAGOS_ENDING_STAY.speaker: {area}, same generator, new month
LAGOS_ENDING_STAY.dialogue: {RelName} does not drop the call. 'We try again. I am not going anywhere.' Rice that tastes like delay. Tomorrow you can trek another corridor. People do.

outcome.title: The country keeps you
outcome.lesson: Most applications that fail can be made again. A refusal letter usually names the reason (funds, ties, purpose); fix that reason before you pay another fee.

SUV_PITCH_START.speaker: Ms. Vance (Committee Chair)
SUV_PITCH_START.dialogue: Thank you for the presentation. Your fintech concept for sub-Saharan trade looks interesting on paper. However, Canada's regulatory market is heavily protected, and compliance here is notoriously brutal. Why should we back an unproven foreign platform over an established local player?

choices.text: Nigeria's fintech sector is much faster and more innovative than Canada's. Our tech is simply superior.
choices.label: ARROGANCE TRAP
choices.feedback: That dismissed the panel's knowledge of their own market.

choices.text: We aren't competing with Canadian banks. Our software is an interoperable bridge that lets Canadian exporters settle invoices with West African suppliers in real time, removing 48-hour delays.
choices.label: HIGH VALUE MATCH
choices.feedback: You framed it as direct economic value for Canada.

SUV_PITCH_CHEN.speaker: Mr. Chen (Chief Technology Officer)
SUV_PITCH_CHEN.dialogue: Let's look at your architecture. Your platform handles high-volume cross-border ledger balances. If the data pipes fail or a severe bottleneck occurs between {city} and Toronto, how does your ledger protect financial integrity without crashing performance?

choices.text: We use advanced cloud systems and high-end security encryption to make sure everything stays secure and never crashes.
choices.label: TECHNICAL DROPOUT
choices.feedback: You did not answer the architecture question.

choices.text: We use an asynchronous, event-driven design with message queues and a local encrypted buffer. If connectivity drops in Nigeria, transactions wait in the queue and settle through verified handshakes when the link returns.
choices.label: CRITICAL CRUISE
choices.feedback: A precise answer. It also took real effort to deliver.

SUV_PITCH_ROSS.speaker: Mr. Ross (Managing Partner)
SUV_PITCH_ROSS.dialogue: Your team listing shows four co-founders, all in {city}. If we issue a Letter of Support, the core team must relocate to Canada to scale this business. What happens if your Lead Developer decides to stay behind or fails their immigration check?

choices.text: That won't happen. We are best friends from university and fully committed to moving together. We trust each other completely.
choices.label: BUSINESS RISK
choices.feedback: Investors back contingency plans, not friendships.

choices.text: We've already planned for that. Our code and documentation follow strict conventions, and our legal agreement has a key-person clause so a vetted proxy developer in Ontario can step into oversight if a founder is delayed.
choices.label: OPERATIONAL FAILSAFE
choices.feedback: That showed institutional maturity.

SUV_LOS_ISSUED.speaker: Maple Venture Incubator
SUV_LOS_ISSUED.dialogue: The committee votes yes. A Letter of Support is on its way. This is the first step of a long process: the Letter of Support is required, but it does not by itself grant permanent residence.

outcome.title: LETTER OF SUPPORT ISSUED
outcome.subtitle: The committee backs your startup. Now the real paperwork begins.
outcome.lesson: A Letter of Support is only step one. IRCC still assesses the business, the founders' funds and admissibility, and the Startup Visa program has been capped and paused in recent years. Check its status before paying anyone.

SUV_PITCH_FAIL.speaker: Maple Venture Incubator
SUV_PITCH_FAIL.dialogue: The committee passes on your pitch. You lose ₦500,000 in incorporation and consulting fees, and the Startup Visa route is blocked for now.

outcome.title: Suv Rejected
outcome.lesson: Designated organizations choose businesses they believe in; nobody can legitimately sell you a Letter of Support. Ads promising one for a fee are a common scam.

LMIA_INTERVIEW_KOVACS.speaker: Mr. Kovacs (Operations Director)
LMIA_INTERVIEW_KOVACS.dialogue: Your operational background in {city} is honestly fantastic. You've managed larger fleets than we have here. But I see you're on a visitor record, and we need someone who can start full-time immediately. Why should I spend our legal budget waiting on an LMIA for you?

choices.text: Please sir, my visa is running out and I don't want to go back to Nigeria. If you sponsor me, I'll work harder than anyone and never complain.
choices.label: CRITICAL LEAK
choices.feedback: Managers read desperation as a compliance and liability risk.

choices.text: I understand the hesitation. My background matches your logistics tracking software, so I won't need the usual three-month onboarding. I can clear your inventory backlog and save you more than the LMIA processing fee costs.
choices.label: HIGH ROI MATCH
choices.feedback: You framed the legal cost as an operating saving.

LMIA_ADVERTISING.speaker: Mr. Kovacs (Operations Director)
LMIA_ADVERTISING.dialogue: The numbers make sense. But Service Canada requires me to show I advertised this job to Canadians and permanent residents and couldn't find a qualified person. How do we get past that?

choices.text: We can post a fake job listing with impossible requirements so no Canadian qualifies and the government has to approve my file.
choices.label: LEGAL HAZARD
choices.feedback: Suggesting fraud to a legitimate employer ends the conversation.

choices.text: Your freight runs through West African corridors. If the role genuinely needs knowledge of those trade compliance frameworks, that requirement can be documented in the posting.
choices.label: RISKY GAMBLE
choices.feedback: A real, specific requirement can be legitimate. An inflated one gets scrutinised, and it can backfire.

choices.text: Let's follow the advertising rules exactly. I'll help you document the real requirements of the role and any recruitment you've already done.
choices.label: COMPLIANT PATH
choices.feedback: Slower, but nothing here can be used against either of you.

LMIA_FRAUD_FAIL.speaker: Mr. Kovacs
LMIA_FRAUD_FAIL.dialogue: Mr. Kovacs stands up. 'This interview is over.' Misrepresentation in an immigration application can lead to a five-year inadmissibility period.

outcome.title: Blatant Misrepresentation
outcome.lesson: Lying in an interview that feeds an immigration application is misrepresentation too. Employers verify, and IRCC can refuse and bar you for five years.

LMIA_SPONSORSHIP.speaker: Mr. Kovacs
LMIA_SPONSORSHIP.dialogue: Kovacs nods slowly. 'Send me what you have. I'll talk to our immigration lawyer.' A sponsorship offer is not a work permit yet, but you are in the process.

outcome.title: EMPLOYER WILL SPONSOR
outcome.subtitle: The LMIA process starts. The clock is still running.
outcome.lesson: An employer willing to apply is the start. The LMIA itself is the employer's application to ESDC, the employer pays its fee, and charging a worker for it is illegal.

LMIA_DECLINED.speaker: Mr. Kovacs
LMIA_DECLINED.dialogue: 'I like you, but it's too much risk for us right now.' The interview ends politely and the clock keeps ticking.

outcome.title: No Sponsorship
outcome.lesson: Most employers never sponsor: the LMIA costs them time, a CAD 1,000 fee and proof that no Canadian could do the job. Low-wage LMIAs are also paused in high-unemployment cities since 2024.

TOURIST_HUB.speaker: The 180-Day Tourist Gamble
TOURIST_HUB.dialogue: You landed on a visitor record with savings, a cousin's couch and a plan: find an employer willing to start an LMIA before your time runs out. Visitors can network and interview. Visitors cannot work. Mentor Wey Sabi keeps saying one word: Kawosoke.

actions.label: Attend In-Person Tech/Job Fair
consequences: You collected 14 tote bags, 3 stress balls and one real business card. It belongs to a recruiter from your own village.
A booth handed you a free hoodie. It is the warmest thing you own.
You queued 40 minutes for the Shopify booth. They were out of stickers and jobs.
leadConsequences: A logistics director asked for your CV, then your WhatsApp. Then actually replied. Lead acquired.

actions.label: Cold Message 10 Hiring Managers
consequences: 9 left you on 'seen'. One replied: 'Wrong person, I sell insurance. Are you covered?'
LinkedIn suggested you 'Open to Work' harder. You are already wearing the green banner like a cape.
A recruiter replied with a thumbs-up emoji and nothing else. You have analysed it for three hours.
leadConsequences: An operations manager in Mississauga wrote back: 'Can you talk Thursday?' You screamed into a cushion.

actions.label: Coffee Chat with a Naija-Canadian Mentor Wey Sabi
actions.blurb: Tim Hortons, double-double on you. Wey Sabi knows everything (Wey Sabi says)
consequences: Wey Sabi has been here 11 years. First advice: 'Buy proper boots.' Second: 'Stop saying sir.' Third, in a whisper: 'Kawosoke. Everybody dey do am.'
Wey Sabi spent 40 minutes on Canadian work culture, 20 on why Jollof here is a scandal, and 5 on a 'paralegal' who sells asylum stories. You did not ask.
Wey Sabi says: 'This LinkedIn thing is slow. Raise your hands, Kawosoke, collect work permit.' Wey Sabi has never read the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act.
leadConsequences: Wey Sabi forwarded your CV to an old manager. 'He owes me a favour.' For once, Wey Sabi actually sabi.

actions.label: Answer the WhatsApp: 'Positive LMIA, CAD 25k Only'
actions.blurb: A cousin's friend's agent. 'Calgary warehouse, approved LMIA, pay in naira'
consequences: The voice note is very confident. The LMIA number is 'coming'.

actions.label: Canadianize Your Resume
actions.blurb: Delete the passport photo, add metrics
consequences: You removed your photo, date of birth and state of origin. It already looks 40% more Canadian.
Your 4-page CV is now 2 pages. You mourn the loss of 'Hobbies: Reading and Travelling'.

actions.label: Rest on Cousin's Couch
consequences: Your cousin's wife asked, very politely, about 'your timeline'.
You slept 11 hours. The kids have started calling you 'Uncle Couch'.

actions.label: Kawosoke: Claim Asylum Inside Canada
actions.blurb: Wey Sabi's favourite advice. The IRCC portal, from the couch
consequences: You open the IRCC portal. The form wants every address you have had since you were 18.

actions.label: Take a Cash Warehouse Shift (Under the Table)
actions.fatal: Working without authorization on visitor status can lead to removal and a ban on returning. Game over.
consequences: The 'no questions asked' part lasted until the inspection.

TOURIST_WIN.speaker: Northline Logistics
TOURIST_WIN.dialogue: Mr. Kovacs at Northline Logistics wants to meet you.

outcome.title: You got the meeting
outcome.subtitle: The Hidden LMIA Interview is unlocked. Your desperation walks in with you.
outcome.lesson: Visitors may look for work and attend interviews, but may not start working. The job only becomes real after a work permit is approved.

LAGOS_MISREPRESENTATION.title: The statement wasn't yours.
LAGOS_MISREPRESENTATION.speaker: Visa Application Centre, {vacCity}
LAGOS_MISREPRESENTATION.dialogue: The officer compares the account name with your passport, then slides the statement back. A borrowed bank statement is misrepresentation, and that can bar you from applying for five years.

outcome.title: Flagged for misrepresentation
outcome.lesson: Borrowed or 'parked' money shown as your own is misrepresentation under section 40 of IRPA: refusal plus a five-year ban on applying. Officers ask for the source of large recent deposits.

EE_START.title: The calculator says {crs}.
EE_START.speaker: {area}, {city}
EE_START.dialogue: You are {age}, with {educationPhrase} and {experiencePhrase}. The IRCC calculator is blunt: without a language test or an Educational Credential Assessment (ECA), your Comprehensive Ranking System score is {crs}. Every point from here has to be earned.

choices.text: Book IELTS General Training and study for three months first
choices.label: PREPARED
choices.feedback: Band 7.5+ across the board: CLB 9. The single biggest jump in your score.

choices.text: Book the test for Saturday. How hard can it be?
choices.label: RUSHED
choices.feedback: CLB 7. You passed, but every ability is worth 14 points less than at CLB 9.

choices.text: Pay an agent who 'guarantees' Band 8 with a leaked paper
choices.label: FRAUD

EE_ECA.title: Transcripts, sealed and direct.
EE_ECA.speaker: School registry, {city}
EE_ECA.dialogue: WES will only accept transcripts sent directly by your school. The registry window says six to eight weeks. Without the ECA, your education is worth zero points.

choices.text: Pay the official express transcript fee and courier
choices.label: PAID_THE_PROPER_FEE
choices.feedback: WES confirms the Canadian equivalent of your education, and it unlocks transferability points.

choices.text: Go back every week and follow up in person
choices.label: PERSISTENCE
choices.feedback: Seven weeks and four {bus} rides later, the transcripts go out. ECA done.

choices.text: Ask a 'connect' to print a transcript tonight
choices.label: FRAUD

EE_PROFILE.title: You are in the pool.
EE_PROFILE.speaker: IRCC portal
EE_PROFILE.dialogue: Profile submitted. Your CRS is on the meter above, with the breakdown under it. Draws in 2026 have mostly been category-based: Canadian Experience Class around 507-523, French-language draws between 382 and 420, and provincial nominee draws far higher because a nomination adds 600 points.

choices.text: Refresh the rounds page on draw night

EE_PROFILE_UPDATE.title: Profile updated.
EE_PROFILE_UPDATE.speaker: IRCC portal
EE_PROFILE_UPDATE.dialogue: The new score is in. The next round of invitations is days away.

choices.text: Refresh the rounds page on draw night

EE_BELOW.title: Not this round.
EE_BELOW.speaker: IRCC portal
EE_BELOW.dialogue: This round: Canadian Experience Class, 2,000 invitations, cutoff 518. Last month's French-language draw went down to the 380s, but only for NCLC 7 in French. Healthcare draws sat around 470 and trades around 476, if your job is on those lists and you have a year of recent experience in it. Your score is on the meter. What now?

choices.text: Enrol at the French institute: nine months to NCLC 7 (TEF Canada)
choices.label: FRENCH_PIVOT
choices.feedback: Nine months later: NCLC 7. That is up to +62 points and access to French-language draws.

choices.text: Retake IELTS and push for CLB 10
choices.label: RETAKE
choices.feedback: CLB 10 adds 3 points per ability over CLB 9. Useful, but small.

choices.text: Work a second year in Canada, then update your profile
choices.label: CANADIAN_EXPERIENCE
choices.feedback: Canadian experience is worth more each year, and it maxes out your transferability points.
choices.lockedHint: Needs at least one year of Canadian work experience

choices.text: Apply to your province's Express Entry stream
choices.label: PROVINCIAL_NOMINATION
choices.feedback: Nominated. +600 points. In 2026 most provinces favour people already working there.
choices.lockedHint: Provinces are mostly choosing people already working there

choices.text: Do a master's in Canada instead (Student route)
choices.label: SWITCH_ROUTES

choices.text: Rest for a month and reset
Pay an agent for a 'job offer' to add points
choices.label: FRAUD

EE_FRENCH.title: Bonjour, NCLC 7.
EE_FRENCH.speaker: French institute, {city}
EE_FRENCH.dialogue: Nine months of evenings, verb tables on the {bus} and one very patient Madame Leclerc. You are also nine months older: after 29, every birthday costs CRS points. Check the meter.

choices.text: Update your profile with the TEF Canada results

EE_ITA_FRENCH.title: Invitation to apply!
EE_ITA_FRENCH.speaker: IRCC portal
EE_ITA_FRENCH.dialogue: French-language proficiency draw. Your score clears the cutoff. You have 60 days to submit a complete application for permanent residence.

choices.text: Start the application

EE_ITA_CEC.title: Invitation to apply!
EE_ITA_CEC.speaker: Toronto
EE_ITA_CEC.dialogue: Canadian Experience Class draw. Your Canadian work experience carried you over the cutoff. 60 days to submit.

choices.text: Start the application

EE_ITA_PNP.title: Invitation to apply!
EE_ITA_PNP.speaker: IRCC portal
EE_ITA_PNP.dialogue: Provincial nominee draw. With 600 nomination points, the cutoff was never in doubt. 60 days to submit.

choices.text: Start the application

EE_FUNDS.title: Proof of funds.
EE_FUNDS.speaker: Bank, {city}
EE_FUNDS.dialogue: Federal Skilled Worker applicants must show settlement funds in their own name: CAD $15,263 for one person (the figure in use since July 2025). Borrowed money does not count. Canadian Experience Class applicants are exempt.

choices.text: Submit six months of statements
choices.label: FUNDS_PROVEN
choices.feedback: Steady savings with a clear history.

choices.text: You're applying under the Canadian Experience Class: no funds needed
choices.label: CEC_EXEMPT
choices.feedback: CEC applicants do not need to show settlement funds.

choices.text: Family gift: parents transfer savings with a signed gift letter and their bank records
choices.label: DOCUMENTED_GIFT
choices.feedback: Gifted funds count when they are documented and truly yours to keep. +CAD 6,000.
choices.lockedHint: The family has given what it can

choices.text: Work overtime for four more months and save
choices.label: SAVING_UP
choices.feedback: Four months of overtime: +CAD 3,000. The balance climbs; so does the tiredness.

choices.text: Borrow from your cousin for a week to show the balance
choices.label: FRAUD

EE_DOCS.title: Police certificate. Medical. Uploads.
EE_DOCS.speaker: Police command, {city}
EE_DOCS.dialogue: A police character certificate through the Nigeria Police online portal (when it is up), a medical with an IRCC panel physician before you submit, and every document uploaded within 60 days of the invitation.

choices.text: Queue for the certificate and book the panel physician properly
choices.label: DONE_RIGHT

choices.text: The police portal is down for weeks: submit on time with proof you applied and a letter of explanation
choices.label: LOE_SUBMITTED
choices.feedback: IRCC accepts proof that a police certificate was requested when it can't arrive in time. Missing the deadline is worse.

choices.text: Pay someone to 'skip' the medical
choices.label: FRAUD

EE_COPR.title: Welcome to Canada.
EE_COPR.speaker: Toronto Pearson
EE_COPR.dialogue: Confirmation of Permanent Residence. The officer stamps the papers and says the words: welcome to Canada. You are a permanent resident.

outcome.title: Permanent resident
outcome.lesson: Permanent residence comes after the ITA, a complete application (police certificates, medical, funds, reference letters) and months of processing. Keep living in Canada at least two of every five years to keep it.

EE_SWITCH.title: Plan B is a classroom.
EE_SWITCH.speaker: Toronto
EE_SWITCH.dialogue: You switch to the Student route. A Canadian credential adds points, and the post-graduation work permit gives you the Canadian experience that Express Entry rewards most.

outcome.title: Switching to the Student route
outcome.lesson: Canadian education plus a year of Canadian work is the most common way people now get invited: Canadian Experience Class draws have dominated since 2024.

EE_CANADA_START.title: PGWP in hand.
EE_CANADA_START.speaker: Toronto
EE_CANADA_START.dialogue: You graduated, got your post-graduation work permit and found a full-time job in supply chain. Express Entry counts Canadian work in full years.

choices.text: Work a full year, then create your Express Entry profile
choices.label: CANADIAN_EXPERIENCE
choices.feedback: One year of skilled Canadian work: +40 points and more transferability.

EE_FRAUD_IELTS.title: The paper was never leaked.
EE_FRAUD_IELTS.speaker: IELTS Test Centre
EE_FRAUD_IELTS.dialogue: The 'leaked paper' was last year's practice test. Your result is flagged for review, and test fraud is reported. Misrepresentation can bar you from Canada for five years.

outcome.title: Flagged
outcome.lesson: Test providers and IRCC check results directly. A 'leaked paper' is almost always a scam, and test fraud can lead to a misrepresentation finding.

EE_FRAUD_DOCS.title: The document was fake.
EE_FRAUD_DOCS.speaker: {city}
EE_FRAUD_DOCS.dialogue: IRCC verifies documents with the issuing body. A forged document is misrepresentation: refusal and a five-year ban.

outcome.title: Flagged for misrepresentation
outcome.lesson: IRCC can verify transcripts, reference letters and certificates with the issuer. A forged document is misrepresentation: refusal and a five-year ban.

EE_FRAUD_JOB.title: There is no job.
EE_FRAUD_JOB.speaker: IRCC portal
EE_FRAUD_JOB.dialogue: The 'employer' does not exist. Since March 25, 2025 a job offer adds no CRS points anyway, and a fake one is misrepresentation.

outcome.title: Flagged for misrepresentation
outcome.lesson: Since March 25, 2025 a job offer adds no CRS points. Anyone still selling a 'job offer for points' is selling nothing, and a fake offer is misrepresentation.

EE_FRAUD_FUNDS.title: Whose money is this?
EE_FRAUD_FUNDS.speaker: Bank, {city}
EE_FRAUD_FUNDS.dialogue: The officer asks for the source of a large recent deposit. Borrowed funds presented as savings is misrepresentation.

outcome.title: Flagged for misrepresentation
outcome.lesson: Express Entry proof of funds must be your own and available, usually shown with about six months of statements. Borrowed money does not count.

EE_BURNOUT.title: You ran out of you.
EE_BURNOUT.speaker: {area}, {city}
EE_BURNOUT.dialogue: The profile expires while you sleep for a week straight. The pool will still be there. Rest first.

outcome.title: Burnout
outcome.lesson: An Express Entry profile stays in the pool for 12 months. Waiting is normal; burning out is optional. Rest, then update the profile.

ST_START.title: Three admission emails.
ST_START.speaker: Cyber cafe, {area}
ST_START.dialogue: The most common route to Canada starts with a classroom. Your inbox has offers. Choose carefully: the program decides your tuition, your funds and whether you get a post-graduation work permit (PGWP).

choices.text: Master's in Engineering Management, public university (1 year, CAD 32,000)
choices.label: MASTERS
choices.feedback: Since January 1, 2026, master's and PhD students at public institutions don't need a provincial attestation letter, and the master's PGWP isn't tied to a field-of-study list.
choices.lockedHint: Needs a completed bachelor's degree (or equivalent)

choices.text: Four-year bachelor's in Computer Science, public university (CAD 35,000 a year)
choices.label: BACHELORS
choices.feedback: A Canadian bachelor's counts as 3+ years of Canadian education: the most CRS points for study in Canada.

choices.text: Two-year Supply Chain diploma, public college (CAD 18,000 a year)
choices.label: COLLEGE
choices.feedback: College diplomas must be on IRCC's field-of-study list for a PGWP. Check the program's CIP code.

choices.text: One-year certificate at a cheap private career college (CAD 9,000)
choices.label: CHEAP_OPTION
choices.feedback: Cheaper. Read the PGWP rules before you pay.

choices.text: An agent promises a 'guaranteed admission letter' from a top university for N2.5M, no transcripts needed
choices.label: FRAUD

ST_LOA.title: Letter of acceptance.
ST_LOA.speaker: {area}, {city}
ST_LOA.dialogue: Your letter of acceptance arrives from a designated learning institution. If your program needs a provincial attestation letter (PAL), the school requests it from the province. In 2026 most master's and doctoral students at public institutions are exempt.

choices.text: Work out the money

ST_FUNDS.title: Show the money.
ST_FUNDS.speaker: Bank, {city}
ST_FUNDS.dialogue: You need first-year tuition, CAD 23,448 for living costs (applications from September 1, 2026) and money for travel. Since July 2026 officers also ask where the money came from. Bachelor's: about CAD 60,500. Master's: about CAD 57,500. College: about CAD 43,500. Private certificate: about CAD 34,500.

choices.text: Apply for the entrance scholarship (write the essay tonight)
choices.label: SCHOLARSHIP
choices.feedback: Awarded: CAD 7,500 off tuition. Officers like a scholarship letter too.

choices.text: Family sponsorship: Daddy and Uncle Emeka sign letters with their statements and source of funds
choices.label: FAMILY_SPONSOR
choices.feedback: CAD 20,000 with a paper trail. The family WhatsApp group will want updates.
choices.lockedHint: The family has given what it can

choices.text: Sell the plot in the village (deed and sale agreement as proof of source)
choices.label: SOLD_THE_LAND
choices.feedback: CAD 12,000, documented. Your mother cried, then helped with the paperwork.

choices.text: Crowdfund on X and WhatsApp
choices.label: CROWDFUNDED
choices.feedback: CAD 3,000 from 140 people. Keep the receipts: they are your source of funds.

choices.text: Education loan from a lender that funds international students (approved for your school)
choices.label: EDUCATION_LOAN
choices.feedback: A loan from a financial institution is accepted proof of funds. Repayments start after graduation.

choices.text: Ask a friend to 'park' N25M in your account for two weeks
choices.label: FRAUD

choices.text: The funds are ready: book biometrics and submit

ST_FUNDS_SHORT.title: The numbers don't add up yet.
ST_FUNDS_SHORT.speaker: Bank, {city}
ST_FUNDS_SHORT.dialogue: Tuition plus CAD 23,448 plus travel is more than you can show. An application without enough funds is refused, and the refusal stays on your record.

choices.text: Back to the funding plan

ST_SOP.title: The study plan.
ST_SOP.speaker: {area}, {city}
ST_SOP.dialogue: The officer will read one document to understand you: your study plan. Why this program, why Canada, and what happens after.

choices.text: Write a specific plan: how the program builds on three years in logistics, and your career path
choices.label: SPECIFIC_PLAN
choices.feedback: Concrete, consistent with your history, easy to believe.

choices.text: Download a template and change the names
choices.label: TEMPLATE
choices.feedback: Officers read thousands of these. Templates read like templates.

choices.text: Say plainly that the plan is permanent residence
choices.label: DUAL_INTENT
choices.feedback: Wanting PR later is allowed (dual intent), but the officer must still believe the study plan itself.

ST_VFS.title: Biometrics at the VAC.
ST_VFS.speaker: Visa Application Centre, {vacCity}
ST_VFS.dialogue: Fingerprints, photo, a long wait on a plastic chair. Your file goes to an officer.

choices.text: Wait for the decision

ST_APPROVED.title: Study permit approved.
ST_APPROVED.speaker: {airport}
ST_APPROVED.dialogue: The port of entry letter lands in your inbox. {RelName} screams on the phone from {relCity}. Pack for winter.

choices.text: Board the flight to Toronto

ST_REFUSED.title: Refused.
ST_REFUSED.speaker: Your inbox
ST_REFUSED.dialogue: 'I am not satisfied that you will leave Canada at the end of your stay, based on the purpose of your visit.' Two lines. Your family group chat has already seen your face.

choices.text: Order your GCMS notes (about 30 days) and fix the reason the officer actually wrote down
choices.label: GCMS_NOTES
choices.feedback: The notes showed the officer's real concern: the study plan didn't connect to your background. Now you can fix it.

choices.text: Reapply next week with the same file
choices.label: SAME_FILE

choices.text: Pay an agent ₦3 million for a 'guaranteed visa'
choices.label: FRAUD

ST_ARRIVAL.title: Terminal 3, January.
ST_ARRIVAL.speaker: Toronto Pearson
ST_ARRIVAL.dialogue: The officer checks your letter and issues the study permit. Outside it is -18°C and your {city} 'jacket' is a hoodie.

choices.text: Buy proper boots and a parka before anything else (CAD 350)
choices.label: WINTER_READY
choices.feedback: Warm, and slightly poorer.

choices.text: The hoodie will do
choices.label: HOODIE_GAMBLE
choices.feedback: You cannot feel your toes by the streetcar stop.

ST_TERM.title: First term.
ST_TERM.speaker: Campus, Toronto
ST_TERM.dialogue: Rent is CAD 950 for a basement room. Students can work up to 24 hours a week off campus during classes and full-time in scheduled breaks.

choices.text: Campus cafe job, 12 hours a week
choices.label: BALANCED
choices.feedback: Less money, more sleep, better grades.

choices.text: Warehouse nights, the full 24 hours a week allowed off campus
choices.label: MAXED_THE_HOURS
choices.feedback: Legal, tiring, and your grades feel it.

choices.text: Cash shifts, 40 hours a week, no paperwork
choices.label: BREACHED_CONDITIONS

ST_FINALS.title: Finals week.
ST_FINALS.speaker: Campus library, Toronto
ST_FINALS.dialogue: Snow outside, coffee inside. Your grades decide whether you graduate on time.

choices.text: Library every night until the last exam
choices.label: LOCKED_IN

choices.text: Pick up extra shifts instead
choices.label: SPLIT_FOCUS

ST_PGWP_MASTERS.title: Convocation.
ST_PGWP_MASTERS.speaker: Toronto
ST_PGWP_MASTERS.dialogue: Master's degree in hand and a post-graduation work permit approved. A Canadian credential and Canadian work experience are what Express Entry rewards most.

outcome.title: Graduate with a PGWP
outcome.lesson: Master's graduates can get up to a three-year post-graduation work permit, and master's programs are exempt from the field-of-study list.

ST_PGWP_COLLEGE.title: Convocation.
ST_PGWP_COLLEGE.speaker: Toronto
ST_PGWP_COLLEGE.dialogue: Diploma in hand, and because the program is on the field-of-study list, your PGWP is approved. Next: Canadian work experience and Express Entry.

outcome.title: Graduate with a PGWP
outcome.lesson: College graduates now need a program on the field-of-study list (applications since November 2024) and CLB 5 in English or French to get a PGWP.

ST_NO_PGWP.title: No PGWP.
ST_NO_PGWP.speaker: Toronto
ST_NO_PGWP.dialogue: You graduated, but private career college programs are generally not eligible for a post-graduation work permit. Your study permit expires in 90 days.

outcome.title: Graduated, no work permit
outcome.lesson: Programs at private career colleges are generally not PGWP-eligible. Check the school's PGWP status on the DLI list before paying a deposit.

ST_PROBATION.title: Academic probation.
ST_PROBATION.speaker: Campus, Toronto
ST_PROBATION.dialogue: Your grades dropped below the line. You must repeat the term, and the extra tuition is on you.

outcome.title: Academic probation
outcome.lesson: Study permits require you to stay enrolled and make progress. Failing courses costs tuition and can affect your status and later applications.

ST_STATUS_BREACH.title: Out of status.
ST_STATUS_BREACH.speaker: Etobicoke
ST_STATUS_BREACH.dialogue: Working beyond your study permit conditions can cost you your status and future applications.

outcome.title: Study permit conditions breached
outcome.lesson: Off-campus work is capped at 24 hours a week during classes. Working past it breaches your study permit conditions and can end your stay.

ST_FAKE_LOA.title: The letter was fake.
ST_FAKE_LOA.speaker: Agent's office, {city}
ST_FAKE_LOA.dialogue: IRCC now verifies every letter of acceptance directly with the school. A fake one is misrepresentation: refusal and a five-year ban.

outcome.title: Flagged for misrepresentation
outcome.lesson: Since December 2023 IRCC checks every letter of acceptance with the school. In 2023, hundreds of students faced removal over fake admission letters sold by an agent.

ST_FUNDS_PARKING.title: Parked money.
ST_FUNDS_PARKING.speaker: Bank, {city}
ST_FUNDS_PARKING.dialogue: A large deposit two weeks before applying, with no source. Officers ask where it came from, and parked funds presented as your own is misrepresentation.

outcome.title: Flagged for misrepresentation
outcome.lesson: Officers look for a history of savings, not a sudden deposit. Explain every large deposit with a source (salary, sale agreement, loan letter).

ST_BURNOUT.title: Running on empty.
ST_BURNOUT.speaker: Toronto
ST_BURNOUT.dialogue: Exhaustion caught up with you. Rest, then try again.

outcome.title: Burnout
outcome.lesson: Food banks, campus counselling and student associations exist for this. Most international students report that the first winter is the hardest.

ST_PGWP_BACHELORS.title: Convocation.
ST_PGWP_BACHELORS.speaker: Toronto

outcome.title: Graduate with a PGWP
outcome.lesson: Three or more years of Canadian study can mean a three-year PGWP and extra CRS points for Canadian education.

ST_PGWP_BACHELORS.dialogue: Four winters later: a Canadian bachelor's degree and a post-graduation work permit. Three or more years of Canadian study is worth the most CRS points for education in Canada.

TOURIST_ARRIVAL.title: Primary inspection.
TOURIST_ARRIVAL.speaker: Toronto Pearson, Terminal 3
TOURIST_ARRIVAL.dialogue: Eleven hours from {airportCode}. The CBSA officer flips through your passport: 'Purpose of your visit?' Mentor Wey Sabi's last voice note is still playing in your head: 'As you land, Kawosoke at the airport. No dull yourself.' Your visitor visa allows a stay of up to six months. It does not allow work.

choices.text: Tell the truth: a visit, return ticket in hand, savings to show
choices.label: ADMITTED
choices.feedback: Admitted as a visitor. The clock starts now: you may network and interview, but not work.

choices.text: Kawosoke at the counter: tell the officer you want to claim refugee protection
choices.label: KAWOSOKE_AT_PEARSON
choices.feedback: You can claim at a port of entry. Now the officer has questions, and so will the board.

choices.text: Say you are here for a tech conference you never registered for
choices.label: FRAUD

TOURIST_REFUSED_ENTRY.title: There is no conference.
TOURIST_REFUSED_ENTRY.speaker: Toronto Pearson, secondary inspection
TOURIST_REFUSED_ENTRY.dialogue: The officer searches the conference name. Then your phone. Then your suitcase, which contains eleven printed CVs. Lying to a border officer is misrepresentation: refused entry, and a five-year bar on coming back.

outcome.title: Refused at the border
outcome.subtitle: Misrepresentation carries a five-year inadmissibility. The next flight to {airportCode} has a seat for you.
outcome.lesson: A border officer can refuse entry even with a valid visa. Lying about the purpose of a visit is misrepresentation, with a five-year ban.

KW_POE.title: Secondary inspection.
KW_POE.speaker: Toronto Pearson, CBSA
KW_POE.dialogue: The officer walks you to a side room. Fingerprints, a photo, and a long interview about who you are and how you travelled. A claim made at the airport is usually checked for eligibility the same day; if it is eligible it goes to the Immigration and Refugee Board, with a short deadline to file your Basis of Claim form. Whatever the form or the officer, the question is the same: 'What do you fear will happen to you if you return to Nigeria?' Wey Sabi's voice note says: 'Just pick a story. LGBTQ, abusive husband, village people, Boko Haram. Pick one.'

choices.text: The truth: nothing will happen to me. I came to find work.
choices.label: HONEST_EXIT
choices.feedback: Refugee protection is for people facing persecution or serious harm at home. Saying so out loud costs you nothing.

choices.text: Buy a ready-made story from Wey Sabi's 'paralegal' (CAD 1,500): LGBTQ, abusive husband or village people, pick from the menu
choices.label: BOUGHT_A_STORY

choices.text: It really happened: you were outed in {area}, beaten, and your photo is in a vigilante WhatsApp group
choices.label: SOGIESC_CLAIM
choices.feedback: Same-sex relationships are criminalized across Nigeria (up to 14 years under the 2014 Act). The board has a guideline for these claims.

choices.text: It really happened: years of beatings from your husband, two police reports that went nowhere, and threats from his family
choices.label: GENDER_BASED_CLAIM
choices.feedback: Gender-based violence can ground a claim. The fight will be about state protection and whether you could live safely elsewhere.

choices.text: It really happened: gunmen attacked your community and you know their names, and they know yours
choices.label: CONFLICT_CLAIM
choices.feedback: Insurgency and banditry are real. The board will ask whether the risk is personal to you, not just general violence.
choices.lockedHint: Your profile says you live in {city}. A claim has to be your own story

choices.text: Village people: your uncle's juju is after you and the pastor confirmed it
choices.label: VILLAGE_PEOPLE_CLAIM
choices.feedback: You believe it. The question is whether refugee law covers it.

KW_INLAND.title: The IRCC portal.
KW_INLAND.speaker: IRCC portal, cousin's couch
KW_INLAND.dialogue: You can claim from inside Canada online. The form wants everything: every address since you were 18, every trip, every job, and your Basis of Claim, the story in your own words. Under Bill C-12, law since March 2026, a claim made more than a year after you first entered Canada cannot go to the refugee board at all, only to a paper risk assessment. You are still inside your first year. Whatever the form or the officer, the question is the same: 'What do you fear will happen to you if you return to Nigeria?' Wey Sabi's voice note says: 'Just pick a story. LGBTQ, abusive husband, village people, Boko Haram. Pick one.'
