choices.label: BOUGHT_A_STORY

choices.text: It really happened: you were outed in {area}, beaten, and your photo is in a vigilante WhatsApp group
choices.label: SOGIESC_CLAIM
choices.feedback: Same-sex relationships are criminalized across Nigeria (up to 14 years under the 2014 Act). The board has a guideline for these claims.

choices.text: It really happened: years of beatings from your husband, two police reports that went nowhere, and threats from his family
choices.label: GENDER_BASED_CLAIM
choices.feedback: Gender-based violence can ground a claim. The fight will be about state protection and whether you could live safely elsewhere.

choices.text: It really happened: gunmen attacked your community and you know their names, and they know yours
choices.label: CONFLICT_CLAIM
choices.feedback: Insurgency and banditry are real. The board will ask whether the risk is personal to you, not just general violence.
choices.lockedHint: Your profile says you live in {city}. A claim has to be your own story

choices.text: Village people: your uncle's juju is after you and the pastor confirmed it
choices.label: VILLAGE_PEOPLE_CLAIM
choices.feedback: You believe it. The question is whether refugee law covers it.

KW_NO_CLAIM.title: No claim.
KW_NO_CLAIM.speaker: Brampton
KW_NO_CLAIM.dialogue: You close the portal. Wey Sabi calls you 'too honest for this country'. Your cousin, quietly, is relieved. The clock is still running and the job fair is still on Thursday.

choices.text: Back to the job hunt

KW_FAKE_STORY.title: The 'paralegal' has a menu.
KW_FAKE_STORY.speaker: A back office, Mississauga
KW_FAKE_STORY.dialogue: He is not a lawyer or a licensed consultant, so nobody regulates what he sells. The story fits on one page. The same page, he admits, has been sold forty times this year; he only changes the names. 'Memorize am. No add, no remove.'

choices.text: File it anyway
choices.label: FILED_A_BOUGHT_STORY
choices.feedback: Filed. Your name, someone else's life.

choices.text: Walk out. The CAD 1,500 is gone, but so is the trap
choices.label: WALKED_AWAY

choices.text: Report him to the College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants
choices.label: REPORTED
choices.feedback: Only lawyers, Quebec notaries and licensed consultants may charge for immigration advice. He is none of those.

KW_FILED.title: Claim received.
KW_FILED.speaker: Downtown Toronto
KW_FILED.dialogue: Eligibility checked. You get a refugee protection claimant document, Interim Federal Health coverage and an immigration medical booking. Then the question nobody prepared you for: where will you sleep tonight? In 2023 claimants slept on the pavement outside Toronto's shelter intake office until churches opened their halls. The hearing is far away: the board's average wait was well over a year in 2025–2026.

choices.text: Find a lawyer through Legal Aid or a refugee clinic
choices.label: REAL_COUNSEL
choices.feedback: A real lawyer reads your form line by line and starts asking for documents.

choices.text: Pay Wey Sabi's 'paralegal' to 'handle everything'
choices.label: PARALEGAL
choices.feedback: He files nothing. You find out three months later.

choices.text: A Nigerian church opens its hall: a cot, jollof on Sundays, and a pastor who knows a legal clinic
choices.label: SHELTER
choices.feedback: Black churches in Toronto housed hundreds of claimants in 2023, until donations ran out.

KW_WAIT.title: Month 6 of the wait.
KW_WAIT.speaker: Downtown Toronto
KW_WAIT.dialogue: Your work permit arrived. So did the winter. Your Basis of Claim form is in a file somewhere at the board, and the hearing date is still a rumour. How do you spend the wait?

choices.text: Work legally on the open work permit: warehouse nights, PSW course on weekends
choices.label: WORKING_LEGALLY
choices.feedback: Legal now. The first paycheque with your own name on it.

choices.text: Take a cash warehouse job before the work permit arrives
choices.label: CASH_JOB

choices.text: Gather evidence: hospital records, police reports, affidavits from witnesses, news from your area
choices.label: EVIDENCE
choices.feedback: Documents from home take months and DHL fees. Each one is a fact the board doesn't have to take on your word.

choices.text: Post your whole claim story on TikTok for sympathy
choices.label: WENT_VIRAL
choices.feedback: Twelve thousand likes. The board can read TikTok too, and the video does not match your form.

choices.text: Fly home for your mother's 60th birthday
choices.label: WENT_HOME

KW_PREP.title: Hearing prep.
KW_PREP.speaker: Refugee clinic, Toronto
KW_PREP.dialogue: The hearing notice came: four weeks. Your counsel puts your Basis of Claim form on the table. 'Read it again. Is every date right?'

choices.text: Go through it line by line and fix the mistakes before the hearing
choices.label: AMENDED
choices.feedback: Correcting the form before the hearing is allowed and looks honest. Surprises at the hearing do not.

choices.text: Memorize it word for word, like a WAEC answer
choices.label: MEMORIZED
choices.feedback: Board members can tell a memory from a script.

choices.text: Skip prep. You know your own life
choices.label: WINGED_IT

KW_HEARING.title: Room 7.
KW_HEARING.speaker: Immigration and Refugee Board, Toronto
KW_HEARING.dialogue: A board member, your counsel, a recorder. The member asks about the night it happened, then asks the same question a different way twenty minutes later. Wey Sabi's advice, in your head: 'Cry small. Add pepper.'

choices.text: Answer what you remember, and say 'I don't remember' when you don't
choices.label: STRAIGHT_ANSWERS
choices.feedback: Gaps you admit are human. Gaps you fill with new details are not.

choices.text: Add a new detail to make it stronger
choices.label: EMBELLISHED
choices.feedback: 'Why is this not in your Basis of Claim form?' There is no good answer to that question.

choices.text: Cry on cue, the way Wey Sabi coached
choices.label: PERFORMED

KW_IFA.title: 'Why not Port Harcourt?'
KW_IFA.speaker: Immigration and Refugee Board, Toronto
KW_IFA.dialogue: The member believes what happened to you. Then the question that decides many Nigerian claims: internal flight alternative. 'Could you live safely somewhere else in Nigeria? Lagos? Abuja? Port Harcourt?'

choices.text: Explain, with your evidence, why they would find you anywhere, or why the law follows you everywhere
choices.label: ANSWERED_IFA
choices.feedback: The board weighs who is after you, how far their reach goes, and whether moving would be reasonable for you.

choices.text: Say Lagos is too expensive and the traffic is wicked
choices.label: TRAFFIC_DEFENCE
choices.feedback: Expensive and annoying is not the same as unsafe or unreasonable.

KW_ACCEPTED.title: Protected person.
KW_ACCEPTED.speaker: Immigration and Refugee Board, Toronto
KW_ACCEPTED.dialogue: The member gives the decision at the end of the hearing: you are a Convention refugee. Your counsel squeezes your hand. Next: apply for permanent residence as a protected person. One warning: do not renew your Nigerian passport and do not fly home for Christmas. Going back can cost you the protection. {RelName} is already crying on the phone from {relCity}.

outcome.title: Protected person
outcome.subtitle: Your real story, told straight, with evidence. Permanent residence is next.
outcome.lesson: Refugee protection rests on a real fear of persecution or serious harm, told consistently and backed by evidence. Protected persons can apply for permanent residence, but returning to the home country or renewing its passport can cost them the protection.

KW_FAKE_EXPOSED.title: Three versions of one night.
KW_FAKE_EXPOSED.speaker: Immigration and Refugee Board, Toronto
KW_FAKE_EXPOSED.dialogue: The member asks the name of the street where it happened. You give the paralegal's version, then your own, then a third. The member has seen this page before, with other names on it. Refused, and found manifestly unfounded: no appeal to the Refugee Appeal Division, and a removal order. Every invented LGBTQ or abuse story makes it harder for real ones to be believed.

outcome.title: Bought story, refused
outcome.subtitle: Manifestly unfounded. No appeal, removal, and the paralegal has already sold your page to someone else.
outcome.lesson: Board members hear the same template stories many times. A fabricated claim can be found manifestly unfounded (no appeal to the Refugee Appeal Division), and fake claims make it harder for real ones to be believed.

KW_VILLAGE_REFUSED.title: The board does not cover village people.
KW_VILLAGE_REFUSED.speaker: Immigration and Refugee Board, Toronto
KW_VILLAGE_REFUSED.dialogue: The member is very polite. Refugee protection covers persecution for race, religion, nationality, political opinion or membership in a particular social group, or a personal risk to life the state can't protect you from. 'Your uncle's spiritual attacks are none of those.' Refused.

outcome.title: Refused: no nexus
outcome.subtitle: Village People Interference: 100%. Appeal options exist, but the juju is not a Convention ground.
outcome.lesson: Refugee protection covers persecution for race, religion, nationality, political opinion or membership in a particular social group, or a personal risk the state can't protect you from. Spiritual attacks rarely meet that test.

KW_REFUSED.title: Refused.
KW_REFUSED.speaker: Immigration and Refugee Board, Toronto
KW_REFUSED.dialogue: The decision comes by mail: the member did not find your account credible. You can appeal to the Refugee Appeal Division, then ask the Federal Court to review it. If those fail, a pre-removal risk assessment, then a removal date. Years, spent on a story that did not hold together.

outcome.title: Refused on credibility
outcome.subtitle: Inconsistencies, embellishments and a TikTok. The appeal clock starts now.
outcome.lesson: Most refused claims fail on credibility: dates, places and details that change between the form, the interview and the hearing. Correct mistakes before the hearing, not during it.

KW_REFUSED_IFA.title: Believed, but refused.
KW_REFUSED_IFA.speaker: Immigration and Refugee Board, Toronto
KW_REFUSED_IFA.dialogue: The member believes you were harmed. But without enough evidence that they could find you anywhere, the member finds you could live safely in another Nigerian city. Internal flight alternative. You can appeal, and your counsel thinks there are grounds.

outcome.title: Internal flight alternative
outcome.subtitle: Believed, refused. More evidence of who is looking for you might have changed it.
outcome.lesson: For many Nigerian claims the deciding question is internal flight alternative: could you live safely in another city? Evidence of who is looking for you, and how far they can reach, decides it.

KW_ABANDONED.title: The owambe was lovely.
KW_ABANDONED.speaker: {airport}
KW_ABANDONED.dialogue: You flew back to the country you told Canada you feared. Leaving ends your claim, and the photos of you dancing at the owambe end your story.

outcome.title: Claim over
outcome.subtitle: Going home to the place you fear tells everyone you don't fear it.
outcome.lesson: Leaving Canada ends a pending refugee claim. Travelling back to the country you fear is strong evidence that you don't fear it.

EE_ITA_HEALTH.title: Invitation to apply!
EE_ITA_HEALTH.speaker: IRCC portal
EE_ITA_HEALTH.dialogue: Healthcare and social services draw. The cutoff landed around 470, far below the general rounds, because Canada needs nurses more than it needs another logistics analyst. 60 days to submit.

choices.text: Start the application

EE_ITA_TRADES.title: Invitation to apply!
EE_ITA_TRADES.speaker: IRCC portal
EE_ITA_TRADES.dialogue: Trades draw. Electricians, welders, plumbers: the cutoff sat around 476 this year. Your certificate finally outranks a master's degree. 60 days to submit.

choices.text: Start the application

ST_PGWP_LANG.title: One more test.
ST_PGWP_LANG.speaker: Test centre, Toronto
ST_PGWP_LANG.dialogue: Since November 2024 a post-graduation work permit needs a language test: CLB 7 for a university degree, CLB 5 for a college program. Your classmate says 'we studied in English, they will understand'. They will not.

choices.text: Book IELTS General Training and prepare for three weeks
choices.label: BOOKED_THE_TEST
choices.feedback: CLB 9. It counts again later for Express Entry.

choices.text: Skip it. Four years in English is proof enough
choices.label: SKIPPED_TEST

ST_NO_PGWP_LANG.title: Missing language test.
ST_NO_PGWP_LANG.speaker: IRCC portal
ST_NO_PGWP_LANG.dialogue: The PGWP application asks for a test result you do not have. Refused. Your study permit expires in weeks, and booking a test now means results after it does.

outcome.title: PGWP refused
outcome.subtitle: No language test, no PGWP. A three-week study plan would have saved two years.
outcome.lesson: Since November 1, 2024 a PGWP needs a language test: CLB 7 for university graduates, CLB 5 for college graduates. Book it before your final term ends.

FY_LANDING.title: Landing day.
FY_LANDING.speaker: Toronto Pearson, Terminal 3
FY_LANDING.dialogue: Welcome to Canada. You have savings, two suitcases and a list of things everyone forgot to tell you: SIN, bank, phone, health card, a place to live, a coat. {RelName} is calling from {relCity}. What do you do first?

choices.text: Get your SIN at the airport Service Canada desk, then open a newcomer bank account this week
choices.label: ADMIN_FIRST
choices.feedback: Your Social Insurance Number lets you work and get paid. Order matters: SIN, bank, phone, then a lease.

choices.text: Buy the best phone plan in the mall so you can call home properly
choices.label: BIG_PLAN
choices.feedback: Video calls home, CAD 95 a month, a two-year contract. Your landlord will still ask for credit history.

choices.text: Winter coat and boots first; everything else can wait a day
choices.label: COAT_FIRST
choices.feedback: Warm feet change everything. A coat drive or thrift store would have halved the bill.

FY_HOUSING.title: Six months upfront.
FY_HOUSING.speaker: Brampton
FY_HOUSING.dialogue: You have no Canadian credit history. The first landlord wants six months' rent in advance. The second listing is a shared basement bed for CAD 375. A Facebook 'landlord' who is 'out of the country' wants a deposit before a viewing.

choices.text: Offer a bank letter, a job-search plan and a guarantor from church
choices.label: GUARANTOR
choices.feedback: First and last month, a reference from someone with Canadian credit. In Ontario, a landlord can't demand more than first-and-last as a deposit.

choices.text: Take the CAD 375 basement bed: three people, one bathroom, no lease
choices.label: BUNK_BED
choices.feedback: Cheap, crowded and often illegal. Cities crack down on overcrowded basements, and you would be the one moving.

choices.text: Send the Facebook 'landlord' a CAD 1,500 deposit so nobody else gets it
choices.label: RENTAL_SCAM
choices.feedback: There was no landlord. Never pay before a viewing, and check that the person owns the property.

FY_JOBS.title: No Canadian experience.
FY_JOBS.speaker: Brampton Public Library
FY_JOBS.dialogue: Application number forty. The rejection says what the last thirty-nine meant: 'We are looking for candidates with Canadian experience.' Back home you were {occupation}. Here, you are a file with no references.

choices.text: Take a warehouse survival job, nights, and keep applying by day
choices.label: SURVIVAL_JOB
choices.feedback: Rent paid. Most newcomers start in a survival job; the risk is staying there by default.

choices.text: Volunteer two days a week and go to every newcomer meetup and church career night
choices.label: NETWORKING
choices.feedback: Most jobs are filled by referral. Volunteering gives you a Canadian reference.

choices.text: Only apply for jobs at your old level, and wait
choices.label: HOLDING_OUT
choices.feedback: Savings drain faster than callbacks arrive. Overqualified newcomers are common; underemployed ones are more common.

FY_CREDENTIALS.title: The credential wall.
FY_CREDENTIALS.speaker: Settlement agency, Mississauga
FY_CREDENTIALS.dialogue: Your counsellor explains: regulated jobs (nursing, medicine, engineering, teaching, law) need a Canadian licence. That can mean assessments, exams and a bridging program, often a year or two. Unregulated jobs need a Canadian-style resume and a referral.

choices.text: Enrol in a bridging program for internationally trained professionals, with a loan
choices.label: BRIDGING
choices.feedback: Slow and expensive, and the fastest legal way back to your profession.

choices.text: Take a PSW or assistant job in your field and study for the exams at night
choices.label: BRIDGE_JOB
choices.feedback: Paid, close to your field, exhausting. Many nurses spend their first years as PSWs.

choices.text: Drive Uber full-time and park the career for now
choices.label: PARKED_CAREER
choices.feedback: Good money this month. Credentials that sit unused get harder to restart.

FY_BLACK_TAX.title: Mummy is calling.
FY_BLACK_TAX.speaker: Your room, Brampton
FY_BLACK_TAX.dialogue: School fees for your sister, and Uncle's hospital bill: ₦1.2 million. The family sold land to send you; you know it, they know it, and nobody says it.

choices.text: Send all of it this week
choices.label: SENT_EVERYTHING
choices.feedback: Family happy, rent at risk. Black tax with no budget eats every pay cheque.

choices.text: Send a fixed share, about 15% of what you earn, every month, and explain the plan
choices.label: FIXED_SHARE
choices.feedback: A set amount the family can rely on and you can afford. Many people keep a separate 'family account'.

choices.text: Say no this time; you are not stable yet
choices.label: SAID_NO
choices.feedback: Rent is safe. The guilt arrives by voice note.

FY_WINTER.title: January.
FY_WINTER.speaker: Brampton
FY_WINTER.dialogue: −28°C with the wind. Dark at 4:45 p.m. You have not spoken to anyone in person in three days. Somebody in the group chat says 'Canada is not for the weak' with a laughing emoji. You are not laughing.

choices.text: Stay inside and scroll until spring
choices.label: HIBERNATED
choices.feedback: Seasonal low mood is common among newcomers, and isolation makes it worse.

choices.text: Join the Nigerian association's winter games night and the church choir
choices.label: FOUND_PEOPLE
choices.feedback: Community is the thing every newcomer says they underestimated.

choices.text: Book a family doctor or walk-in visit about your mood (covered by your health card)
choices.label: GOT_HELP
choices.feedback: Talking to a doctor about low mood is routine here. Many provinces also run free counselling lines.

FY_WORK_EVENT.title: Month nine.
FY_WORK_EVENT.speaker: Mississauga
FY_WORK_EVENT.dialogue: The contract you finally got ends early: 'restructuring'. The job market has been rough for newcomers since 2024. Your team lead says you were good. Good is not the same as kept.

choices.text: Apply for Employment Insurance and use the weeks to retrain
choices.label: EI_AND_RETRAIN
choices.feedback: If you worked enough insurable hours, EI is yours. It exists for exactly this.

choices.text: Move to a cheaper province where your field is short of workers
choices.label: MOVED_PROVINCE
choices.feedback: Cheaper rent and a real job offer, far from everyone you know. {RelName} in {relCity} offers a couch.

choices.text: Take any shift on any app this week
choices.label: ANY_SHIFT
choices.feedback: Rent paid. The resume gap grows.

FY_DECEMBER.title: Detty December is calling.
FY_DECEMBER.speaker: Brampton
FY_DECEMBER.dialogue: Flights to {airportCode} are CAD 2,400. Your friends are posting countdowns. The IJGB ('I Just Got Back') season starts in two weeks. Someone asks if you are 'coming home for good'.

choices.text: Stay. Save for next year and keep building
choices.label: STAYED
choices.feedback: One quiet December, one step closer. Most first years end like this.

choices.text: Go home for December as an IJGB and spend big
choices.label: IJGB
choices.feedback: Jollof, owambe, your mother's face. And January's rent.

choices.text: Go home for good
choices.label: WENT_HOME

FY_FIELD.title: Back in your field.
FY_FIELD.speaker: Downtown Toronto
FY_FIELD.dialogue: A referral from someone you met at a potluck, a Canadian reference from your volunteering, a licence exam passed. The offer letter has your real job title on it.

outcome.title: Back in your field
outcome.subtitle: Year One done. Your career is moving again.
outcome.lesson: Credential recognition and the 'Canadian experience' gap take most skilled newcomers a year or more. Bridging programs, volunteering and referrals are what shorten it.

FY_SURVIVING.title: Surviving.
FY_SURVIVING.speaker: Brampton
FY_SURVIVING.dialogue: Rent paid, family helped, savings small but alive. Your career is on pause, not over. Year two is when people either climb or settle.

outcome.title: Surviving, not thriving
outcome.subtitle: You made it through Year One. Now plan the climb.
outcome.lesson: Statistics Canada finds immigrants with foreign degrees are about twice as likely to be overqualified for their jobs. Most climb out by planning it: licensing, bridging, networking.

FY_JAPADA.title: Japada.
FY_JAPADA.speaker: {airport}
FY_JAPADA.dialogue: You land at {airportCode}. The heat hits like a hug. The group chat says 'reverse japa' like it's a scandal. Your mother says nothing and cooks.

outcome.title: Reverse japa
outcome.subtitle: You went home. It is allowed.
outcome.lesson: About one in five immigrants leaves Canada within 25 years (Conference Board, 2025). Permanent residents must live in Canada two of every five years to keep PR; citizenship keeps both doors open.

FY_BURNOUT.title: Out of everything.
FY_BURNOUT.speaker: Brampton
FY_BURNOUT.dialogue: Money, sleep, patience: all gone at once. You call {relName}, who says the thing nobody said before you came: 'Everybody's first year is like this. Nobody posts it.'

outcome.title: Year One won
outcome.subtitle: Rest, then try again with help.
outcome.lesson: Newcomers in their first five years have had far higher unemployment than people born in Canada. Settlement agencies, food banks, EI and free counselling exist for the hard months; using them is not failure.

ST_REFUSED_AGAIN.title: Refused again.
ST_REFUSED_AGAIN.speaker: Your inbox
ST_REFUSED_AGAIN.dialogue: Same file, same officer reasoning, same two lines. Another application fee gone.

outcome.title: Refused twice
outcome.subtitle: A refusal tells you what to fix. Fix it first.
outcome.lesson: Insufficient funds and 'not satisfied you will leave' are the most common reasons Nigerian study permits are refused. GCMS notes show the officer's actual reasoning; read them before you pay another fee.

ST_AGENT_SCAM.title: The agent's phone is off.
ST_AGENT_SCAM.speaker: {area}, {city}
ST_AGENT_SCAM.dialogue: The office is now a phone repair shop. The 'guaranteed visa' was a PDF. You are one of about forty people outside with the same receipt.

outcome.title: Scammed by a 'guaranteed visa'
outcome.subtitle: Nobody can guarantee a Canadian visa.
outcome.lesson: IRCC and the Nigeria Police warn that anyone promising a guaranteed visa is a scammer. Only lawyers and licensed consultants (check the CICC register) may charge for immigration advice.

ST_HOUSING.title: Where will you sleep?
ST_HOUSING.speaker: Brampton
ST_HOUSING.dialogue: Your residence application was waitlisted. A listing offers a bunk bed in a shared basement for CAD 375 with three post-dated cheques and no lease. A Nigerian church's student fellowship offers two weeks with a host family while you search.

choices.text: Two weeks with the church host family, then a proper room near campus
choices.label: HOST_FAMILY
choices.feedback: Jollof on day one, a lease on day twelve. Community networks meet students at the airport for a reason.

choices.text: Take the CAD 375 bunk bed: you are here to save money
choices.label: BUNK_BED
choices.feedback: Six people, one bathroom, one fire exit. Overcrowded basements are a known risk for international students.

choices.text: Pay a CAD 1,500 deposit to a Facebook landlord you haven't met
choices.label: RENTAL_SCAM
choices.feedback: He blocked you after the e-transfer. Never pay before a viewing.

EE_REFERENCE.title: Write it yourself.
EE_REFERENCE.speaker: Your old office, {city}
EE_REFERENCE.dialogue: Every job you claim needs a reference letter: dates, hours, salary and your actual duties, on letterhead, signed. Your former boss says, 'You know what you did. Just write it and I'll sign.'

choices.text: Write your real duties in your own words; your boss signs on company letterhead
choices.label: REAL_DUTIES
choices.feedback: Duties that match the NOC in substance, written about your actual job. That is what officers want to see.

choices.text: Copy the NOC duties word for word so it matches perfectly
choices.label: COPIED_NOC
choices.feedback: Officers know the NOC text by heart. A letter that reads exactly like it invites questions.

choices.text: Leave that job out to save time
choices.label: DROPPED_A_JOB
choices.feedback: Fewer points, and an employment history that doesn't match your earlier visa files.

EE_PFL.title: Procedural fairness letter.
EE_PFL.speaker: IRCC portal
EE_PFL.dialogue: 'We have concerns that the duties described in your reference letter were copied from the National Occupational Classification. You have 30 days to respond.' A PFL is not a refusal yet. It is a chance.

choices.text: Hire a licensed consultant or lawyer and send pay slips, tax records and a corrected letter in your own words
choices.label: ANSWERED_PFL
choices.feedback: Evidence that the job was real answered the concern.

choices.text: Ignore it and hope it goes away
choices.label: IGNORED_PFL

choices.text: Ask a 'connect' for a backdated 'clarification letter'
choices.label: FRAUD

EE_PFL_REFUSED.title: Refused.
EE_PFL_REFUSED.speaker: IRCC portal
EE_PFL_REFUSED.dialogue: Thirty days passed. The officer decided on the file as it was: refused. The invitation is gone; the pool is waiting again.

outcome.title: Refused after a PFL
outcome.subtitle: A procedural fairness letter is the officer asking for your side.
outcome.lesson: A PFL gives you a deadline (often 30 days) to answer a concern before a decision. Answering with real evidence often saves the file; silence almost never does.

TR_LMIA_SELLER.title: 'Positive LMIA, CAD 25k only.'
TR_LMIA_SELLER.speaker: WhatsApp, cousin's couch
TR_LMIA_SELLER.dialogue: He sends a PDF on old letterhead and a voice note: 'Calgary warehouse, approved LMIA, half now, half when you land the work permit.' Wey Sabi says his cousin did it.

choices.text: Pay the first CAD 12,500 before someone else takes it
choices.label: PAID_FOR_LMIA

choices.text: Ask for the employer's legal name and the LMIA number, then check the company yourself
choices.label: VERIFIED
choices.feedback: He stopped replying after the second question. Workers never pay for an LMIA; the employer applies and pays the fee.

choices.text: Report the ad to the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre and warn the family group chat
choices.label: REPORTED
choices.feedback: Two cousins thank you. One forwards it anyway.

TR_LMIA_PAID.title: The LMIA was never real.
TR_LMIA_PAID.speaker: WhatsApp
TR_LMIA_PAID.dialogue: The 'LMIA' number belongs to a bakery in Halifax. The agent's WhatsApp picture is now a sunset. Your savings went with it.

outcome.title: Paid for an LMIA
outcome.subtitle: Workers never pay for an LMIA.
outcome.lesson: Charging a worker for an LMIA or a job offer is illegal in Canada; the employer applies to ESDC and pays the CAD 1,000 fee. Since March 2025 a job offer adds no Express Entry points either.

KW_CAUGHT.title: A tip to CBSA.
KW_CAUGHT.speaker: Warehouse, Etobicoke
KW_CAUGHT.dialogue: A co-worker you argued with makes a call. Working without a permit while your claim is pending gets you a removal order and a very difficult conversation with your lawyer.

outcome.title: Caught working without a permit
outcome.subtitle: Wait for the permit. It usually comes.
outcome.lesson: Refugee claimants can get an open work permit once the claim is eligible and the medical is done. Working before that is unauthorized work, and enforcement often starts with a tip.
